trajectory_summary: This is a flat, checklist-driven call: the rep moved through verify items efficiently but never built energy, never flipped the bill or reason into leverage, and let a shaky bill-commitment and unlocked time slip through at the very end. The customer was cooperative throughout, so the call never had to fight resistance, but it also never generated any pull toward the appointment beyond mechanical scheduling.
outcome_dispute: v1 tag unknown; observed outcome should be tentative, not booked, because the appointment is explicitly conditioned on the customer sending the bill ('I'm not able to put you in the schedule until I get that') and the customer's own commitment is hedged ('I probably could... I'll know that tomorrow').

observed_outcome.quote: I'm not able to put you in the schedule until I get that. So I'll just shoot you a text.
observed_outcome.reasoning: A specific time (9am customer's time) was agreed, but the rep explicitly states the customer isn't yet in the schedule pending the bill, making this a conditional/tentative set rather than a locked booking.

bill_anchor_audit.reasoning: Bill was captured at 01:39 ('150,') but acknowledged only with '32. Okay. Cool.' at 01:42; the flip should have gone here, reflecting the bill back as pain worth solving before moving to the credit qualifier.

interest_reason_audit.reasoning: Customer stated 'we're saving some money' at 00:34 as their reason, but the rep never referenced this again — not at scheduling, not at button_up, not in the close.
